title: The Body
human_question: What is this body we live in, and whose is it?
journey: Chathura meets bodies at work and in time: farmers, labourers, athletes, healers, elders, the sick.
surface: Strength, labour, ageing, illness and care, with the body's texture seen without sentimentality.
depth: The twenty-eight kinds of matter and the four great elements. Matter has four origins (kamma, mind, temperature, nutriment), so the body is partly made by mind and past action. Matter never arises alone (kalāpa). Decay and impermanence are written into matter's own definition. Body contemplation and breathing turn this into direct seeing.

arc.opening: A body shaped by work or time. Object 7 is acquired here.
arc.middle: Elements, senses, growth, ageing and care, seen through physical lives.
arc.closing: Every body ends, and the question becomes what continues.

hands_off: The body ends, so what carries on?

concepts.role: The four great elements: earth (hardness), water (cohesion), fire (heat), air (motion).
The five sense objects: the material world as it meets the senses.
The ten non-concrete kinds of matter, including space, bodily and vocal expression, growth, decay and impermanence.
Classifying matter: internal and external, gross and subtle.
The four origins of matter: kamma, mind, temperature, nutriment.
Material groups (kalāpa): matter never arises alone.
How matter occurs through a life, from conception onward.
The cessation of matter at death.
Contemplating the body's thirty-two parts: seeing the body without its story.
Mindfulness of breathing: the body's most ordinary rhythm as a way in.

lesson.in_simple_terms: The body we call ours is kept going, moment by moment, by many things at once: what came before, the mind, warmth and food. The same warmth that grows it also wears it out, and at the end its renewal stops piece by piece. The texts suggest looking at it closely, part by part and breath by breath, to see it as it is.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: අප 'මගේ' යයි කියන ශරීරය මොහොතින් මොහොත පවත්වා ගන්නේ පෙර කර්මය, සිත, උණුසුම හා ආහාරය යන හේතු රැසක් එකට ක්‍රියා කිරීමෙනි. එය වඩන උණුසුමම එය දිරවන අතර, අවසානයේ එහි අලුත්වීම පිළිවෙළින් නතර වේ.
lesson.the_teaching: The Abhidhamma counts matter in twenty-eight kinds resting on four great elements, hardness, cohesion, heat and motion, which never arise alone but always in small bound groups together with colour, smell, taste and nutritive essence. Bodily matter has four origins, past action, mind, temperature and food: mind-born matter moves the body and holds its posture, and the body's lightness and ease come and go with sleep, food, weather and mood. The same heat that ripens a young body wears an older one down, and decay belongs to all matter, with grey hair only its sign. Reciting the body's thirty-two parts and counting the breath are the texts' ways of turning this inventory into direct seeing. At death the streams of matter stop in a fixed order, and only temperature-born matter continues in the corpse.
progression: EPD-0058 Before First Light: the body stays upright only while a waking mind holds it up, and its lightness depends on sleep, food and weather.
EPD-0059 Counting to Ten: steady counting, the texts' own paddy-measurer image, keeps attention and a working body in one place.
EPD-0060 The Kiln and the Hand: all matter is the four great elements, always together, differing by proportion and changing when conditions change.
EPD-0061 Two Kinds of Sound: one kind of sense object, sound, can come from two different makers, a meaning mind or the weather.
EPD-0062 What the Eye Receives: seeing rests on a small sensitive part of the body, and the senses are what we grip most tightly as 'mine'.
EPD-0063 Learning the Body: reciting the thirty-two parts turns one body called 'mine' into a list, loosening the single label.
EPD-0064 Eleven Weeks: a body is assembled out of sight as the origins of matter join in order, then kept going as an unbroken stream.
EPD-0065 Two Bodies, One Warmth: one ripening warmth builds a young body and wears an old one down; decay was there all along.
EPD-0066 What the Fire Doesn't Take: at death the streams of matter stop in order, and only what heat and cold do remains.
lesson.builds_on: The kindness group showed goodness arriving as a team of factors, among them lightness, pliancy and ease; this group follows kindness to the body it must care for, and finds that the body too is a team, kept going by many conditions and able to give way at any point.
lesson.hands_to_next: If a body stops in layers and nothing in it goes on being renewed, what, if anything, continues, and how is the end of one life linked to what follows?
